title: docs/userguide/tasks.rst#task-naming-relative-imports section is misleading
body:

# Description

As of 3cf5072ee5f95744024f60e0f4a77eb2edb8959f, [Tasks § Automatic naming and relative imports][1] states:

https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/3cf5072ee5f95744024f60e0f4a77eb2edb8959f/docs/userguide/tasks.rst#L260-L266

However, it goes on to say:

https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/3cf5072ee5f95744024f60e0f4a77eb2edb8959f/docs/userguide/tasks.rst#L309-L313

Hence, the documentation is inconsistent in saying whether or not new-style relative imports lead to inconsistent automatic task name generation for tasks contained within the imported module.

# Suggestions

- **Celery 5.x**: Celery 5.0 dropped support for Python 2 and only supports Python 3. Since Python 3 does not support old-style relative imports, the entire section can be dropped.
- **Celery 4.x**: Change the description to the following:

  > For example if the client inside the ``"myapp"`` module imports the module ``"myapp.tasks"`` as ``"tasks"``, and the worker imports the module as ``"myapp.tasks"``, the generated names won't match and an :exc:`~@NotRegistered` error will be raised by the worker.

[1]: https://docs.celeryproject.org/en/master/userguide/tasks.html#automatic-naming-and-relative-imports
